where: Section 1, paragraph starting 'Non-factorability is the definition'
problem: The claim 'Tracing out Bob leaves Alice with the mixed state I/2, the maximally mixed state' is presented as a general property of entangled states. It holds only for the maximally entangled (Bell) states. A general entangled state such as (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√(2−ε)... i.e. any state with unequal Schmidt coefficients, gives a reduced state that is mixed but not I/2; for example √0.9|00⟩+√0.1|11⟩ leaves Alice with diag(0.9, 0.1). A student will carry away the wrong rule that every entangled qubit looks locally maximally mixed.
fix: Say: 'For the Bell states below the reduced state is I/2, the maximally mixed state, and that is why Alice's local measurement looks perfectly random. A general entangled state gives a reduced state that is mixed but not necessarily I/2; only maximally entangled states give I/2.'

problem: No-cloning is stated for 'an unknown entangled qubit', which wrongly suggests the restriction is special to entangled qubits. The theorem applies to any unknown quantum state.
fix: 'An unknown quantum state cannot be copied, and this includes a qubit that is part of an entangled pair; see the No-cloning theorem chapter.'
